audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim at the stated preprint pages (7, 27, 45) of the held Creissels OUP sketch; zero 'stress'/'accent' tokens in that text. The deciding source is a 2024 handbook sketch, but it is by the language's principal describer, and the underlying 370-pp reference grammar (Creissels & Biaye 2016, Glottolog's top grammar for bala1302) is openly posted on the author's site; I downloaded it to Its phonology chapter has consonants, vowels, tones (binary H/B, contour tones as BH/HB on one syllable, downstep, floating L), syllable structure and liaison, with no stress/accent section and no prosodic use of 'accent' anywhere in the book: it confirms the 'tonal, no word stress described' coding exactly. The grammar also notes Fudeman 1999 ignores tone and describes a semi-speaker, so no competing English source is likely to overturn this.

tone.quote: Comme un certain nombre d’autres langues tonales d’Afrique sub-saharienne, le balante ganja fait un usage particulier des distinctions tonales dans le système verbal. Pour les autres catégories de mots, le ton a une valeur lexicale, c’est-à-dire que chaque lexème a son propre contour tonal qui contribue à le distinguer d’autres lexèmes de la même catégorie. ... dans le système verbal, chacun des éléments grammaticaux qui entrent dans la composition des formes verbales a un ton qui lui est propre ..., mais toutes les bases verbales ont le même contour tonal haut avec un élément bas final.
tone.locator: section 'Éléments de grammaire', §2 'Le système verbal' (fiche unpaginated)
tone.translation: Like a number of other tone languages of sub-Saharan Africa, Balante Ganja makes a particular use of tonal distinctions in the verb system. For the other word categories, tone has a lexical value, i.e. each lexeme has its own tonal contour which helps distinguish it from other lexemes of the same category. ... in the verb system, each of the grammatical elements entering into the make-up of verb forms has its own tone ..., but all verb bases have the same high tonal contour with a final low element.
